statement: GitLab has been an all-remote company since its founding, with no company offices; its roughly 2,000 team members work from more than 60 countries.

GitLab runs on a public handbook that serves as the single source of truth for how the company operates. Team members work handbook-first (document it in the handbook before acting on it) and asynchronously by default, with meetings as a last resort.
In March 2020 GitLab published a free remote work playbook to help companies switching to remote work for the first time during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Automattic, the company behind WordPress.com, WooCommerce and Tumblr, is a fully distributed company. In April 2025 it laid off about 16% of its staff (roughly 280 people), cutting headcount from 1,777 to about 1,495.
In 2017 Automattic closed its 15,000-square-foot San Francisco office because almost no one used it; about five people typically came in.

Doist, the maker of Todoist, has been a remote company since 2011 and runs an async-first culture in which no one is expected to be online at set times. Its team of around 100 people is spread across dozens of countries.
From 1995 through the end of 2025 the FDA cleared or approved about 1,430 AI-enabled medical devices, almost all through the 510(k) pathway.
source: AuntMinnie (analysis of the FDA AI-enabled device list)

statement: Radiology dominates FDA-authorized AI devices: 1,094 of the 1,430 AI-enabled devices authorized from 1995 through 2025 (76.5%) were in radiology, such as tools that read X-rays, CT scans and mammograms or flag urgent findings.
source: AuntMinnie (analysis of the FDA AI-enabled device list)

statement: On December 4, 2024 the FDA finalized guidance on predetermined change control plans (PCCPs) for AI-enabled device software. A PCCP lets a manufacturer pre-authorize planned model updates in its original submission instead of filing a new marketing application for each change.

On January 7, 2025 the FDA issued draft guidance, 'Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions: Lifecycle Management and Marketing Submission Recommendations', covering transparency, bias, data quality, human factors and cybersecurity across the device's total product lifecycle.

In the Swedish MASAI randomized trial of 80,033 women, AI-supported mammography screening detected 20% more cancers than standard double reading by radiologists, without raising false positives, and cut radiologists' screen-reading workload by 44%.

Telehealth visits in the first quarter of 2020 were 50% higher than in the same period of 2019, and 154% higher in the last week of March 2020 than in the same week of 2019, according to data from four large US telehealth providers.

By mid-2021 US telehealth use had stabilized at about 38 times its pre-pandemic level, at 13-17% of office and outpatient visits, down from a peak of about 32% in April 2020. Uptake was highest in psychiatry (50%) and substance use disorder treatment (30%).
Of US private-sector business establishments opened in March 2013, 79.6% survived their first year, 50.6% were still operating after five years and 34.7% after ten years.

Intuit agreed in September 2021 to buy Mailchimp for about $12 billion, the largest sale of a bootstrapped tech company. Mailchimp was founded in 2001, never took venture capital, and had about $800 million in revenue in 2020.

Global venture funding totaled about $425 billion in 2025, up 30% from $328 billion in 2024 and the third-highest year on record after 2021 and 2022. Roughly half of it, about $211 billion, went to AI companies.

In April 2024 NASA said the existing Mars Sample Return plan was unaffordable: Administrator Bill Nelson said an $11 billion budget was too expensive and a 2040 return date too far away, and NASA asked industry for cheaper, faster proposals.

In January 2025 NASA said it would study two Mars Sample Return landing architectures, a sky crane design costing $6.6-7.7 billion and a commercial lander costing $5.8-7.1 billion, with a decision expected in 2026 and samples returning as early as 2035.

Congress's fiscal 2026 appropriations, enacted in January 2026, declined to fund the existing Mars Sample Return program and instead provided $110 million for a 'Mars Future Missions' line. No approved mission remains to bring Perseverance's samples back to Earth, so no Mars Sample Return launch is scheduled.
Bitcoin reached a record of about $69,000 on November 10, 2021. It did not exceed that level again until March 2024.
Bitcoin crossed $100,000 for the first time on December 5, 2024, after rising from about $69,000 on the day of the US presidential election in November 2024.

Bitcoin's highest price in 2025, and its all-time high, was just over $126,000 in early October 2025. It never reached $200,000, fell to about $107,000 within days of the peak, and ended 2025 lower than it started.
In September 2026 bitcoin traded around $86,000, its highest level since January 2026 and still well below its October 2025 record of about $126,000.
